newsitem.title: USA: Carnival unit says bookings up 37 pct.
newsitem.headline: Carnival unit says bookings up 37 pct.

text.p: Bookings at Carnival Cruise Lines, the main unit of Carnival Corp, are up 37 percent in the three months through last Monday versus a year ago and shipboard berths are up 13 percent, Carnival Cruise Lines President Robert Dickinson said on Wednesday.
"Occupancy is at 110 percent, because we do a lot of families," Dickinson told Reuters after a presentation at the Seatrade Cruise Shipping Convention here.
Young children typically share rooms with their parents.

Dickinson said Carnival Cruise Lines now operated the Carnival Destiny, the largest cruise ship afloat, but that the net increase in berths was just 13 percent. He credited a new television advertising campaign in the United States with much of the increase.
Other industry executives speaking here are reporting strong bookings like Carnival, the largest cruise company.
Dickinson said during a panel appearance that Carnival had record finanancial results last year. "We're on track to exceed those records in 1997," he said.
